ai.definition: Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) refers to an artificial intelligence system that can understand, learn, and apply knowledge to any intellectual task at a level comparable to human intelligence.
ai.howItWorks: AGI operates through sophisticated machine learning algorithms and cognitive architectures designed to mimic the human brain's ability to process information, reason, and solve complex problems. It involves deep neural networks, symbolic reasoning, and possibly reinforcement learning to enable a wide range of cognitive functions.
ai.problemSolved: Current AI systems are often limited in their application areas; AGI aims to address this by creating an AI that can perform any intellectual task as well as or better than humans across the board.
ai.manufacturing: The development and deployment of AGI would require significant advancements in hardware, such as more powerful CPUs, GPUs, and specialized neuromorphic chips. Software-wise, it involves complex algorithms and cognitive models.
ai.buildProcess: Building an AGI system involves developing advanced machine learning frameworks, creating large-scale datasets for training, and integrating various AI techniques to ensure the system can handle a wide range of tasks autonomously.
ai.costDrivers: Key cost drivers include the development of sophisticated hardware, the creation of vast amounts of high-quality data, and the ongoing research needed to improve AGI capabilities. Additionally, the energy consumption required for training and running such systems is also a significant factor.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: While AGI is not yet fully developed, it is considered near-term with ongoing advancements in AI technology.
ai.regulation: Current regulatory frameworks are insufficient to address the potential impacts of AGI. There is a need for new policies and guidelines to ensure ethical use and safety.
ai.risks: Risks include the potential loss of jobs due to automation, ethical concerns related to decision-making processes, and the possibility of unintended consequences if AGI systems are not properly controlled.
ai.profitability: The profitability of AGI is difficult to predict but could be immense given its wide-ranging applications in industries such as healthcare, finance, and autonomous vehicles. However, significant investment and time would be required before any financial returns can be realized.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will likely focus on improving the generalization capabilities of AI systems, enhancing their ability to handle unstructured data, and ensuring safety and ethical considerations are addressed.

glossary.def: An AI system capable of performing any intellectual task at a level comparable to human intelligence.
A subset of AI that involves algorithms and statistical models that enable systems to improve their performance on a specific task through experience.
Frameworks designed to model the cognitive processes of humans, enabling AI systems to perform tasks in a manner similar to human cognition.

subsystems.name: Core model
subsystems.role: a large neural network trained on broad data to predict and generate patterns across domains.

subsystems.name: Memory and knowledge
subsystems.role: stores facts and experiences, and retrieves them when needed.

subsystems.name: Reasoning and planning
subsystems.role: breaks problems into steps, searches over possibilities, and verifies solutions.

subsystems.name: Learning and adaptation
subsystems.role: updates the system from new experience without forgetting old skills.

subsystems.name: Perception and action
subsystems.role: connects the system to the outside world through sensors and actuators.

subsystems.name: Safety and alignment
subsystems.role: keeps the system’s goals and actions consistent with human intent.

buildSteps.title: Collect and curate data
buildSteps.detail: Gather text, images, code, audio and other modalities from diverse sources, then filter for quality, bias and legal use.

buildSteps.title: Train a foundation model
buildSteps.detail: Use self-supervised learning on massive compute to build a single model that can represent many kinds of information.

buildSteps.title: Add memory and retrieval
buildSteps.detail: Connect the model to an external knowledge store so it can recall facts and past interactions without retraining.

buildSteps.title: Integrate reasoning modules
buildSteps.detail: Wrap the model with search, planning and verification loops so it can solve multi-step problems rather than just predict the next token.

buildSteps.title: Enable continual learning
buildSteps.detail: Design algorithms that let the system absorb new experience and skills over time without catastrophic forgetting.

buildSteps.title: Ground in the world
buildSteps.detail: Give the system tools, APIs and robotic actuators so it can test hypotheses and act on its plans.

buildSteps.title: Align and oversee
buildSteps.detail: Fine-tune behaviour with human feedback, build interpretability tools, and run red-team evaluations to catch unsafe or deceptive tendencies.

buildSteps.title: Evaluate broadly
buildSteps.detail: Test performance across a wide battery of cognitive tasks—language, maths, science, social reasoning, creativity—and iterate until it matches human level across the board.

prerequisites.why: training the largest models requires tens of thousands of specialised chips running for weeks.
broad competence depends on exposure to varied text, images, code and interaction logs.
current models still fail at long chains of logic, planning and causal inference.
models lack a stable, long-term memory that updates with experience.
we cannot yet reliably steer or understand the internal goals of large models.
no agreed test defines human-level performance across all cognitive domains.

pathway.milestone: Large language and multimodal models that can hold conversations, write code and reason in short bursts
pathway.unlocks: useful assistants for search, drafting and simple automation.

pathway.milestone: Agentic systems that plan and execute multi-step tasks over hours or days
pathway.unlocks: reliable automation of complex workflows in software and robotics.

pathway.milestone: Continual learning and robust memory, so systems improve from experience without retraining from scratch
pathway.unlocks: personalised, adaptive AI that accumulates expertise.

pathway.milestone: Integration of all components into a single system that matches human performance across cognitive domains
pathway.unlocks: accelerated scientific discovery and general-purpose autonomous problem-solving.
